about.title: Avalon Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Avalon's small, close-knit healthcare setting on Santa Catalina Island means most residents rely on a limited number of providers and, often, transport to the mainland for specialized care. When something goes wrong during that care chain — a delayed diagnosis, a medication mix-up, or a preventable complication during transfer — the effects can be serious and long-lasting. California's MICRA law governs these cases with a strict discovery-based filing window, a required 90-day pre-suit notice, and a mandatory qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was actually breached. A bad medical outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the law requires showing a provider fell below what a reasonably careful practitioner would have done. If you believe medical negligence affected your care in Avalon, our team can review what happened and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: What Avalon Patients Should Know Before Moving Forward

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to file a medical malpractice claim. Missing either deadline can end your case before it starts.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Is Required First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must be given 90 days' written notice. Our team is familiar with this step and can make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Testimony Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: California law requires a qualified medical expert to establish that a provider's care fell below the accepted standard. We can help determine whether your situation meets that threshold.

items.question: Is a bad result from treatment automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful practitioner would have done in the same situation. A poor outcome alone, even a painful one, doesn't establish negligence without that proof.

items.question: Does living on Catalina Island affect my malpractice case?
items.answer: It can affect logistics, since Avalon residents often depend on a small set of local providers or transfers to mainland hospitals for advanced care. Our team is familiar with island healthcare arrangements and can help sort out which providers or facilities may be involved in your claim.

items.question: How much money can I recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: California's MICRA law caps non-economic damages, though that cap increases each year under current law. We can walk you through how the current cap applies and what economic damages might also be available.
